work_completed: Verified the supplied probe against npm otoi 1.2.0, a build of main, and PyPI nlt-otoi 1.2.0: an inline personal source in a charter overrides the host's personal document, and the SPEC section 7 privacy floor is not implemented.
Made both ports consume the toi package's APIs: canonicalize for leaf equality, parseToi on host documents, isSigned and verifyToi on signed documents, compareTier, and TOI_RESERVED_PREFIX.
Fixed two leaf-equality bugs: npm false conflicts on key order, and Python missing true vs 1 conflicts.
Raised the @neurolift-technologies/toi range to >=1.0.1 (package version; the .toi format version stays 1.0.0).
decisions_made: Unsigned documents are still accepted; only a present $signature that fails verifyToi is rejected.
An undefined leaf is treated as not stated in conflict detection, matching resolveToi.
No package version bump in this PR; validating host documents suggests a minor release.
decisions_pending: Same-tier override by an unsigned inline personal charter source: put host documents first, require signatures for personal charter sources, or both.
SPEC section 7 privacy floor: pick the most restrictive value on same-tier privacy disagreement, or fail closed.
Whether to use toi DEFAULT_DOCUMENT as default platformDefaults; Python nlt-toi 1.0.0 lacks it, so it would need adding there first.
SPEC section 8 wording that names npm package version 1.0.1 inside a format-level rule.
npm otoi 1.2.0 was published from 8337a9c, a pre-squash commit of PR #43 on no branch, without a provenance attestation.
handoff_record.next_agent_notes: The original override still reproduces after this PR because the injected document is unsigned; that is intended until Joshua decides the pending items. The asfdk packages re-export otoi and will pick up a release through their version ranges. asfdk separately has an unreleased crisis-routing fix (asfdk #41).
